body:
Implement Enabling team visual representation

This change adds the Enabling team type from Team Topologies to the PlantUML extension. The Enabling team is now properly represented with dark purple styling that matches the book's conventions.

Key improvements:
- Add Enabling team color definition (#673AB7, dark purple)
- Create two Team_Enabling macro variants:
  - Basic: alias and label only
  - Extended: includes description support
- Apply consistent styling with:
  - Dark purple background with darker border (#5E35B1)
  - White text for better readability on dark background
  - Rounded corners (20px)
  - Proper text formatting and padding

The implementation follows the same pattern established for Stream-aligned and Platform teams, maintaining consistency across team types.

Resolves: #TT-004

author: mgross21
body:
This pull request introduces several changes across documentation, styling, Python dependencies, and error handling in the codebase. Key updates include adding instructions for building documentation locally, improving the CSS for better readability and customization, updating Python version requirements, and simplifying error handling in the `loader.py` file.

### Documentation Updates:
* Added a new section in `CONTRIBUTING.md` with instructions for building the documentation locally using `sphinx-build`. This includes commands to generate and view the HTML documentation.
* Updated the table of contents in `CONTRIBUTING.md` to include the new "Building the Documentation Locally" section.

### Styling Enhancements:
* Overhauled `docs/_static/custom.css` to include better organization with thematic sections for layout, links, tables, syntax highlighting, and more. Updated link colors and added styles for syntax highlighting and footer navigation buttons. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2ed9e487689006f9987e65a4e62763cb6580f6197ddb9e4c752e20850e8880d9L9-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2ed9e487689006f9987e65a4e62763cb6580f6197ddb9e4c752e20850e8880d9L22-R86) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2ed9e487689006f9987e65a4e62763cb6580f6197ddb9e4c752e20850e8880d9L60-R220)

### Dependency Updates:
* Updated Python version requirements in `pyproject.toml` from `>=3.9,<4.0` to `>=3.11,<4.0` and changed the Python dependency version from `^3.10` to `^3.11`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L27-R27)
* Added `sphinx` and `sphinx-rtd-theme` as dependencies in `pyproject.toml` to support documentation building.

### Code Simplification:
* Simplified error handling in the `loader.py` file by replacing specific exception handling with a generic `Exception` raise. This reduces redundancy in error messages.

### Configuration Changes:
* Disabled built-in Pygments styles in `docs/conf.py` to allow full customization via CSS.

body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the `AstronomyPictureOfTheDay` project, including enhancements to functionality, dependency updates, and new methods for fetching data. The most important changes include adding support for fetching NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) by a specific date, updating package dependencies across multiple projects, and removing outdated test-related packages.

### Functional Enhancements:

* Added a new method `GetPictureByDateAsync` to the `INasaPictureOfTheDay` interface for fetching APOD by a specific date. This method has been implemented in the `NasaPictureOfTheDay` class, enabling date-based API calls. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c39deec50bbefb2210309b110ef5dd72a948c6f7f000423344e30e8b09675b02R11)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f88d4708e46906d7b061f2f657092e0a05c9289930b36cba396d3fec56a2a91cR84-R114)`)
* Introduced `GetAPODByDateJsonAsync` in the `IRestServiceCaller` interface and its implementation in `RestServiceCaller` to support the new date-based APOD functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-37dc9fea04b26115324a5b7045487b7485e0b398921b9aac80883015a69ffff3R12)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ab8d7eba3fbffc19d02a60efba9044f6943d7de8f35d36125e8ba425a522a0ebR28-R34)`)
* Updated the `MainWindowViewModel` to use the new `GetPictureByDateAsync` method for fetching today's APOD, improving code clarity and flexibility. (`[AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Sample.Avalonia/ViewModels/MainWindowViewModel.csL80-R80](diffhunk://#diff-d15746c8be7f43fd33da645be836dddd8ef5aa759040ee2cbdbb741ffe519cf0L80-R80)`)

### Dependency Updates:

* Updated Avalonia-related packages (`Avalonia`, `Avalonia.Desktop`, `Avalonia.Themes.Fluent`, `Avalonia.Fonts.Inter`) to version `11.3.0` in `AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Sample.Avalonia.csproj`. (`[AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Sample.Avalonia/AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Sample.Avalonia.csprojL24-R34](diffhunk://#diff-114f598c72e031b9482c92b73fe66be79f8bc5e460e28f11a4af045a744324e6L24-R34)`)
* Updated several shared dependencies (`Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Http`, `System.Text.Json`) to version `9.0.5` across all project files. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-114f598c72e031b9482c92b73fe66be79f8bc5e460e28f11a4af045a744324e6L24-R34)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2e149709c44e355f51cb606b8318949594ed922eabfefb5b3652c54119643a62L10-R22)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d3853b767883823d395fd07269a4848f0fd3f7efbf0ad9795a441ed66ff41599L39-R45)`)

### Test Project Cleanup:

* Removed outdated test-related packages (`coverlet.collector`, `coverlet.msbuild`) from `AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Xunit.Tests.csproj`. (`[AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Xunit.Tests/AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Xunit.Tests.csprojL10-R22](diffhunk://#diff-2e149709c44e355f51cb606b8318949594ed922eabfefb5b3652c54119643a62L10-R22)`)
* Updated `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` to version `17.14.0` and other testing-related packages (`xunit.runner.visualstudio`, `xunit.v3`) to their latest versions. (`[AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Xunit.Tests/AstronomyPictureOfTheDay.Xunit.Tests.csprojL10-R22](diffhunk://#diff-2e149709c44e355f51cb606b8318949594ed922eabfefb5b3652c54119643a62L10-R22)`)

author: hazelrat
body:
Adds a few new recipes to the biogenerator in the interest of making the hydroponicist more useful, including synthetic blood which I didn't notice had been removed until now.

Fixes broken handheld icons for horticultural magazines, and introduces a simple set of handhelds for them.

Fixes dyn cartons being invisible out of the Condimaster.

Adds sounds for watering, weeding, and sampling hydroponics trays, in addition to a one second timer for weeding and sampling specifically. Intended to add more feedback to hydroponics work - right now it's very mute and lacking in visible messages.

Adds a new functionality to hatchets! They can now uproot plants, killing them instantly, on a two second timer. This is to avoid the tedious and arthritis inducing process of clicking on a single tray several times to kill one plant.

Transitioned some tray documentation to DMDocs.

author: benjyw
body:
An `@rule` can be annotated with `polymorphic=True`, in which
case, if it has a param of a union base type B, then calling it by
name with an instance of M which is a member type of B, 
will dispatch to a `@rule` with the same output type
and a param of type M.

This is the call-by-name equivalent of union Gets.

The "vtable" (mapping from member type to rule 
implementation for that member type) is computed automatically.
This has the advantage that those existing rules, currently
called via union Get, do not need to be modified or annotated.

There may however need to be small changes to rule structure
to ensure that there is a matching rule for each union member.
You can see an example in this PR.

This PR applies this functionality to three very different cases:
PackageFieldSet, GenerateSourcesRequest and GenerateTargetsRequest.

author: nicunursekatie
body:
This commit implements a significant refactoring of the application to improve modularity, performance, and maintainability.

Key changes include:

1.  **View Component Extraction (`App.tsx` Refactor):**
    *   Extracted main application views (Dashboard, All Tasks, Projects, Categories, Calendar, Daily Planner, Settings) from the monolithic `App.tsx` into their own dedicated components (e.g., `DashboardView.tsx`, `AllTasksView.tsx`, etc.).
    *   `App.tsx` now primarily handles routing/view switching, global elements (header, modals), and overall state management, delegating view-specific rendering to these new components.

2.  **Lazy Loading of Views:**
    *   Implemented `React.lazy` and `Suspense` for all extracted view components in `App.tsx`. This defers the loading of each view's code until it is actively navigated to, improving the application's initial load time.

3.  **`TaskList.tsx` Optimization:**
    *   Centralized task editing: Removed the inline editing form from `TaskList.tsx`. Task edits initiated from the list now use the main editing modal controlled by `App.tsx`, ensuring a consistent UX and simplifying `TaskList.tsx`.
    *   Extracted task item rendering logic into a new `TaskItem.tsx` component.
    *   Applied `React.memo` to `TaskItem.tsx` to prevent unnecessary re-renders of individual task items, which is especially beneficial for long lists.

4.  **Custom Hooks Optimization (`useCallback`):**
    *   Wrapped functions returned by custom hooks (`useTasks.ts`, `useProjects.ts`, `useCategories.ts`) with `useCallback` and appropriate dependency arrays.
    *   This stabilizes these functions when passed as props, making `React.memo` on child components (like `TaskItem`) more effective and reducing unnecessary re-renders.

5.  **Date Logic and Task Filtering Review:**
    *   Consolidated common date comparison utility functions (`isDateBefore`, `isDateBetween`) into a new `src/utils/dateUtils.ts` file.
    *   Updated `DashboardView.tsx` and `App.tsx` to use these centralized date utilities.
    *   Refined the filtering logic for `upcomingTasks` in `DashboardView.tsx` for better clarity, consistency, and robustness, using the new date utilities.

These changes aim to make the codebase more organized, easier to maintain, and provide a smoother user experience by optimizing rendering and initial load times.

body:
## Issues Fixed

### 1. Water Ration Tracker Bug
**Problem**: When visiting the town well for the first time, the system incorrectly showed "You have taken 1 ration(s) today" even though the player hadn't actually collected any water yet.

**Root Cause**: The `visitWell()` method was calling `takeWaterRation()` to check the player's current status, but this method actually executes the water taking action instead of just checking the status.

**Solution**: 
- Created a new read-only `checkWaterRationStatus()` method that only queries the database without modifying any data
- Updated `visitWell()` to use this new method for status checking
- The tracker now correctly starts at 0 and increments to 1 only AFTER the player actually takes their first water ration

### 2. Build Button Enhancement
**Problem**: After contributing Action Points to a construction project, the build button would disappear completely, forcing players to run the `/build` command again to contribute more.

**Solution**:
- Build buttons now remain available continuously until the project is completed
- Added a "Add 5 AP" button option when the player has ≥5 AP and the project needs ≥5 AP
- Added real-time Action Point display showing the player's remaining AP
- Both buttons update their enabled/disabled state based on current player AP after each contribution

## Technical Changes

```typescript
// Before: visitWell() incorrectly took water when checking status
const { success: canTake, message, rationsTaken } = await constructionService.takeWaterRation(player.id, cityId);

// After: visitWell() now only checks status without taking water
const { canTake, message, rationsTaken } = await constructionService.checkWaterRationStatus(player.id, cityId);
```

```typescript
// Before: Build buttons disappeared after contribution
await interaction.update({ embeds: [embed], components: [] });

// After: Build buttons remain available with updated status
const row = new ActionRowBuilder<ButtonBuilder>()
  .addComponents(
    new ButtonBuilder()
      .setCustomId(`build_project_${projectId}`)
      .setLabel('🔨 Add 1 AP')
      .setDisabled(currentAP < 1)
  );

if (remainingAp >= 5) {
  row.addComponents(
    new ButtonBuilder()
      .setCustomId(`build_project_5ap_${projectId}`)
      .setLabel('⚡ Add 5 AP')
      .setDisabled(currentAP < 5)
  );
}
```

## Files Modified
- `src/commands/well.ts`: Updated to use read-only status checking
- `src/services/construction.ts`: Added `checkWaterRationStatus()` method
- `src/handlers/buildHandler.ts`: Enhanced with continuous building and 5 AP functionality

Fixes #150.

author: stuntmonkey4u
body:
This commit significantly refactors the Ansible playbook for network forensic inventory. The changes enhance its professionalism, functionality, maintainability, and adherence to best practices.

Key improvements include:

1.  **Report Templating and Output:**
    -   Standardized HTML report template handling using relative paths.
    -   Improved HTML report structure with a summary section and tables for better data presentation.
    -   Ensured temporary host-specific JSON reports are created with secure permissions (0600).

2.  **Playbook Refactoring:**
    -   Organized tasks into logical blocks with clear names and tags.
    -   Added comments to explain complex tasks and logic.
    -   Ensured consistent use of `changed_when: false` for read-only tasks.
    -   Reviewed and confirmed appropriate use of `ignore_errors: true` and `failed_when: false` for robust data gathering.

3.  **Data Collection:**
    -   Standardized installed package collection to use `ansible.builtin.package_facts`, removing redundancy.

4.  **Ansible Best Practices & Linting:**
    -   Applied Fully Qualified Collection Names (FQCN) for all Ansible modules.
    -   Corrected YAML truthy values (yes/no to true/false).
    -   Used `ansible.builtin.command` instead of `ansible.builtin.shell` where appropriate.
    -   Made shell pipes safer using `set -o pipefail`.
    -   Addressed file permission warnings by setting explicit modes.
    -   Introduced an `.ansible-lint` configuration file to manage linting rules, skip false positives (e.g., Docker's Go template format) and intentionally accepted deviations (e.g. `command-instead-of-module` for `systemctl` for simplicity in this context).
    -   Resolved numerous other linting violations, resulting in a clean linting pass according to the project's defined standards.

5.  **Documentation:**
    -   Significantly updated `README.md` with comprehensive details on features, prerequisites, usage, output, and customization.

(This is a re-submission attempt after a minor modification to ensure changes are propagated.)

author: liudf0716
body:
… in auth sync.

This change addresses a potential double-free issue related to client node copies created in `ev_fw_sync_with_authserver` (firewall.c) and processed by callbacks in `centralserver.c`.

The core changes are:

1.  **`centralserver.c` (`process_auth_server_counter`, `client_counter_request_reply`):**
    *   I removed calls to `client_free_node(client)` where `client` was obtained from `context->data`. These callbacks now only use the client data but do not manage the lifecycle of the client node copy itself.
    *   This ensures that the client node (which is a copy from the `worklist` in `ev_fw_sync_with_authserver`) is not freed by the callback.

2.  **`firewall.c` (`ev_fw_sync_with_authserver`):**
    *   This function is now solely responsible for the lifecycle of the `worklist` (a duplicated list of clients) and all its nodes.
    *   It ensures `client_list_destroy(worklist)` is called at the end of the function.
    *   It does not call `client_free_node()` for nodes from `worklist` within its loop, even in error conditions like `get_auth_uri()` failure or `wd_make_request()` failure. These nodes are now correctly cleaned up by `client_list_destroy(worklist)`.

This revised approach centralizes the memory management of the `worklist` nodes within `ev_fw_sync_with_authserver`, preventing double-frees that could occur if both the callback and `client_list_destroy` attempted to free the same client node copy.

author: delorenj
body:
The memory bank path was previously only initialized when the memory bank was explicitly set up. This caused issues when other operations, such as querying the memory bank, were used before this setup, as they would not find the memory bank path even if it was specified in the `.memorybankconfig` file.

This commit fixes the issue by initializing the `MEMORY_BANK_DIR` global variable at startup. The application now reads the `.memorybankconfig` file when the script starts and sets `MEMORY_BANK_DIR` if `bankPath` and `bankName` are present. This ensures that the memory bank path is available globally, allowing all operations to correctly access the memory bank using the configured path without requiring explicit initialization.

author: windriderqc
body:
Refactors Esp32::applyIOConfiguration to accept a const String& containing the JSON configuration, instead of a const JsonDocument&. The function now performs its own parsing of this string into a local JsonDocument.

This change is a diagnostic measure to address a persistent issue where a JsonDocument, appearing correct in the calling function (loadAndApplyIOConfig), would lead to an "'io_pins' is missing" error within applyIOConfiguration.

By making applyIOConfiguration parse the JSON string itself, we ensure the JsonDocument it operates on is created and managed entirely within its own scope, eliminating potential issues related to passing JsonDocument objects by reference in this specific context (such as subtle internal state or data pool lifetime problems).

The calling function loadAndApplyIOConfig has been updated to serialize its (correctly parsed) JsonDocument into a string and pass this string to applyIOConfiguration.
The saveAndApplyIOConfiguration function was also updated to pass a string to applyIOConfiguration.

Summary -
This pull request introduces support for uploading entire folders of audio files, addressing [Issue #45](https://github.com/freeman-jiang/beatsync/issues/45). This feature simplifies the audio uploading process by allowing users to select and upload multiple files from a directory in one action.

![Beatsync feat  Upload Folder](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13478b6e-e05b-4225-8ba5-8e6acfe31bd8)

🎯 What’s New
✅ Implemented folder upload functionality using <input type="file" webkitdirectory>

📁 Users can now upload multiple audio files from a folder at once

🔄 Automatically handles nested folder structures and filters valid audio files

💡 Improved UX by reducing the need for repetitive single uploads

🧪 How to Test
Click the new "Upload Folder" button or select a folder via the updated file input
All valid audio files inside the folder will be selected for upload

⚠ Notes
This implementation uses the webkitdirectory attribute which is currently supported in most Chromium-based browsers

Future enhancements can include drag-and-drop support or recursive folder handling via File System Access API (for browsers that support it)

📌 Related Issue
Closes #45

body:
This commit refactors the database migrations for the `users` and `vulnerabilities` tables to include recently added columns directly into their initial `create_table` migrations. This is done to maintain a cleaner migration history as the database schema is still under initial formulation.

Changes:
- Modified `0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php` to directly include the `last_login_at` (nullable timestamp) column.
- Modified `2025_05_20_041848_create_vulnerabilities_table.php` to directly include the `resolved_at` (nullable timestamp) column.
- Removed the separate migration files:
    - `2025_06_02_025717_add_last_login_at_to_users_table.php`
    - `2025_06_02_025947_add_resolved_at_to_vulnerabilities_table.php`

The associated application logic (models, observers, services, tests) for these columns remains the same as in the previous commits they were introduced in, but this commit ensures the database schema definition is more atomic for these tables during early development.

You might be surprised to learn that Python's built-in XML libraries are [considered insecure](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.html#xml-vulnerabilities) against various kinds of attacks.

In fact, the [Python documentation itself](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.html#the-defusedxml-package) recommends the use of [defusedxml](https://pypi.org/project/defusedxml/) for parsing untrusted XML data. `defusedxml` is an [open-source](https://github.com/tiran/defusedxml), permissively licensed project that is intended as a drop-in replacement for Python's standard library XML parsers.

This codemod updates all relevant uses of the standard library parsers with safe versions from `defusedxml`. It also adds the `defusedxml` dependency to your project where possible.

The changes from this codemod look like this:
```diff
- from xml.etree.ElementTree import parse
+ import defusedxml.ElementTree

- et = parse('data.xml')
+ et = defusedxml.ElementTree.parse('data.xml')
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file.

author: sunkthought
body:
Smart Information Sufficiency: Implemented information sufficiency scoring that considers query component coverage and confidence of addressed components, moving beyond simple confidence metrics.
Dynamic Convergence Detection: MinionS can now detect diminishing returns by tracking per-round information gain, novelty of findings, and task failure trends. This allows the system to stop early if further rounds are unlikely to yield significant new information, especially when sufficiency is met.
Adaptive Thresholds: Key decision thresholds (for confidence-based early stopping, sufficiency requirements, and novelty sensitivity in convergence) are now dynamically adjusted based on:
Document size (small, medium, large).
Query complexity (simple, medium, complex).
First-round performance (high novelty can relax subsequent sufficiency needs).
Performance Profiles: Introduced 'high_quality', 'balanced', and 'fastest_results' profiles to allow users to easily tune the base operational parameters (max rounds, base thresholds) before adaptive adjustments.
Comprehensive Performance Report: The final output now includes a detailed report summarizing total rounds, stopping reasons, final sufficiency and convergence scores, and the effective thresholds used during the run.
Numerous new valves added to configure these adaptive behaviors, convergence criteria, and performance profiles.

author: bettageorge
body:
Especially when using multiple monitors, I am not a fan of EXWM automatically switching X windows to `char mode` upon entering full screen. I understand the reasoning and think it should remain the default, since the unprepared user might otherwise accidentally open an invisible `M-x` menu behind their video player and become very sad.

However, I would argue that users who know what they are doing should have the option of staying in `line mode`. Personally, I often have a full screen video player or game running on one monitor while also using a chat client on another monitor, and if the game is in char mode, I cannot use my regular keybinds to quickly reply to chat messages. I do not want to add those keybinds to `exwm-input-global-keys` since that would mess up my workflow in windows where I enter `char mode` on purpose.

I think adding a customise option for this is a small change that has a benefit for at least some users at essentially no performance impact.

PS: Please let me know if in the future I should open an issue first rather than creating a pull request immediately.

author: shinnkka
body:
Reverts Dansoftowner/jSystemThemeDetector#41

Using the original GNOME support works across all Linux desktop environments .You only need to install `gsettings-desktop-schemas`.

If PR #41 is used, it will introduce the following issues:

1. Desktop environments other than GNOME and KDE Plasma 5, which originally worked, will no longer be supported.

2. Any version of Plasma other than KDE Plasma 5 (nowadays mostly Plasma 6) will enter an infinite error loop, because the environment detection treats all Plasma versions as Plasma 5 without checking the actual version. This leads to missing command errors.

3. The command `kreadconfig5 --file kdeglobals --group General --key ColorScheme` (or `kreadconfig6`) can only retrieve the name of the current color scheme, but it cannot determine whether the scheme is light or dark. The dark theme I’m currently using, _Apus_, does not contain the word "dark" in its name, and is therefore mistakenly identified as a light theme, which is absurd.

🛠️ PR: Implement Code-Splitting with React.lazy + Suspense
🔍 Summary
This PR introduces code-splitting to improve performance by lazily loading route components using React.lazy and React.Suspense. This reduces the initial bundle size and improves app load time.

✅ Implemented Features
Lazy-loaded route components (Home, CreateUser, EditUser)
Loading state handled via Suspense with a reusable spinner UI
Clean and scalable folder structure maintained
No breaking changes — everything works as before, but more performant

author: eddielf
body:
Partially reverts https://github.com/populationgenomics/seqr/pull/260

The variant search results displays the text "gnomAD v4" next to the allele frequency that's in our callsets. At present, our callsets contain gnomAD v3 frequencies, not v4. Until we update this in our callsets, the text displayed in seqr should say "gnomAD v3", to avoid any confusion.

author: nharring-adjacent
body:
This commit introduces a GitHub Action workflow to measure code coverage and provide insights on Pull Requests.

Key changes:
- Added `pytest-cov` to development dependencies for generating coverage data.
- Updated the `python-app.yml` workflow:
  - Modified the pytest execution to collect coverage information for the `src` directory and output it in XML (cobertura) format.
  - Added a step to upload the `coverage.xml` report as a workflow artifact for inspection.
  - Integrated the `MADLAD/publish-coverage-check` action to:
    - Post a comment on Pull Requests detailing the code coverage.
    - Highlight changes in coverage for existing code.
    - Report the coverage percentage for new code introduced in the PR.
- Granted `pull-requests: write` permission to the workflow to allow commenting.

This setup aims to provide developers with timely feedback on how their changes impact code coverage, without enforcing strict coverage gates.

body:
<!--- See CONTRIBUTING.md for general guidelines on contributions -->

## What does the pull request do?
Monitors `firstResponder` property of the Window than determining `firstResponder` via `hitTest` method of `AvnView`. This fixes the root cause of focus issues by preventing unexpected elements from being reported as firstResponder.


## What is the current behavior?
<!--- If the PR is a fix, describe the current incorrect behavior, otherwise delete this section. -->


## What is the updated/expected behavior with this PR?
<!--- Describe how to test the PR. -->


## How was the solution implemented (if it's not obvious)?
The `[AvnView hitTest:]` method sometimes gets executed even when mouse is hovered on some PowerPoint controls. This causes unexpected shifting of focus to the elements that are not really first responders. I believe this is the reason that in Oak `WindowFocusManager` class there are code to check and correct the focus.

Instead of using hitTest, if we use the firstResponder property of the window, we will always get the correct firstResponder. Additional checks in the  WindowFocusManager are not necessary. And fixes the root cause of all focus issues.

author: fintelia
body:
The `CHUNK_BUFFER_SIZE` constant was set to 32KB which applied to two rather different buffer sizes:
1. The buffer that the `StreamingDecoder` uses to read metadata chunks into.
2. How much the `ZlibStream` object grows its output buffer by each time it fills up.

There's no particular reason that these should be the same size. For (1) I wasn't able to tell any performance different with different sizes so I set it to 128 bytes to reduce the amount of memory allocated when starting the decoder.

Decreasing the size used by `ZlibStream` seems to significantly improve performance. On my machine decoding the qoi-bench corpus, I saw a ~2.5% improvement in average end-to-end PNG decoding speed and a nearly 5% improvement in the geomean speed.

author: kiwina
body: # PR for FileWatcher Leak (file-watcher_93) This PR addresses the potential `FileSystemWatcher` leak identified in `leak-report/guaranteed/file-watcher_93.md`. ## Description The `FileWatcher` creates a `FileSystemWatcher` that might not be disposed if the `CodeIndexManager`'s disposal chain is interrupted. While `CodeIndexManager` is added to `context.subscriptions` (which should ensure its `dispose` method is called on extension deactivation), this patch aims to add robustness to the disposal process within the `CodeIndexOrchestrator` as a defensive measure. The proposed fix involves ensuring `CodeIndexOrchestrator` has an explicit `dispose` method that reliably calls `stopWatcher()` (which in turn disposes the `FileWatcher`). ## Related Bug Report Closes: #4230 ## Changes - Added/Updated `dispose()` method in `src/services/code-index/orchestrator.ts` to ensure `stopWatcher()` is called. - Ensured `CodeIndexManager.dispose()` calls the orchestrator's dispose method if available (this might be redundant but adds safety). - [ ] Add/update unit tests if applicable to verify disposal chain. ## How to Test 1. Verify that `CodeIndexManager.dispose()` is called upon extension deactivation. 2. Trace the disposal calls: `CodeIndexManager.dispose()` -> `CodeIndexOrchestrator.stopWatcher()` (or `dispose()`) -> `FileWatcher.dispose()`. 3. Simulate scenarios where extension deactivation might have errors to see if the watcher is still disposed of (this might be hard to test directly). ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes potential `FileSystemWatcher` leak by ensuring proper disposal in `CodeIndexOrchestrator` and `CodeIndexManager`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Ensures `CodeIndexOrchestrator.dispose()` calls `stopWatcher()` to dispose `FileWatcher`. > - `CodeIndexManager.dispose()` now checks and calls `CodeIndexOrchestrator.dispose()` if available. > - **Code Changes**: > - Added `dispose()` method in `orchestrator.ts` to call `stopWatcher()`. > - Updated `dispose()` method in `manager.ts` to ensure orchestrator disposal. > - **Testing**: > - Verify disposal chain: `CodeIndexManager.dispose()` -> `CodeIndexOrchestrator.stopWatcher()` -> `FileWatcher.dispose()`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=RooCodeInc%2FRoo-Code&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 5014270ba36050cad9c91707a118a22607ba76ba. author: lmpulsive
body:
This commit introduces a Gradio-based web interface for the Singing Voice Conversion (SVC) application, packaged within a Docker container for ease of deployment, particularly targeting Hugging Face Spaces.

Key features and changes include:

- Gradio Application (app.py):
  - Allows you to upload an acapella audio file.
  - Select a target speaker from available pre-trained embeddings.
  - Adjust pitch shift.
  - Performs SVC inference and presents the output audio.
  - Includes user feedback and error handling mechanisms.

- Dockerfile:
  - Sets up a Python environment with all necessary dependencies.
  - Copies project code and pre-trained models (Whisper, Speaker Encoder, exported MaxGAN generator maxgan_g.pth).
  - Configured to run the Gradio application on startup.
  - Assumes CPU by default, with notes for GPU adaptation.

- Hugging Face Space Preparation:
  - A new README.md tailored for Hugging Face Spaces, including usage instructions, model information, performance notes, ethical considerations, and YAML metadata for Space configuration.
  - Configuration for git-lfs to handle large model files.

- Workflow:
  - The Gradio app calls existing project scripts (whisper/inference.py, pitch/inference.py, svc_inference.py) as subprocesses to perform the necessary steps for voice conversion (PPG extraction, pitch extraction, and SVC synthesis).
  - Path management and CWD (Current Working Directory) for these scripts are handled within app.py to ensure they function correctly within the Dockerized environment.

This provides an accessible way to demonstrate the core singing voice conversion functionality of the project.

body:
This pull request introduces several updates to the `examples/aip-agent-quickstart` package, focusing on improving code readability, simplifying logging, and adding a new weather tool. The most notable changes include the addition of a new weather tool (`adk_weather_tool.py`), removal of unnecessary logging and comments, and consistent formatting improvements across multiple files.

### New Feature:
* Added `adk_weather_tool.py` to define a weather tool for retrieving detailed weather information for specified cities. This includes temperature, conditions, and humidity, with robust error handling and logging. (`examples/aip-agent-quickstart/aip_agent_quickstart/tools/adk_weather_tool.py`)

### Code Simplification:
* Removed verbose comments and logging statements from various `hello_world_a2a` example scripts, such as `hello_world_a2a_google_adk_client.py`, `hello_world_a2a_google_adk_client_agent.py`, and others, to streamline the code and improve readability. * Consolidated and reformatted `logger.info` statements into single-line formats for cleaner logging in `server.py`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4bd0e97c067d2ba626205ba002118e4636cb8549f6e32b1515cefb8ae7139512L61-R59) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4bd0e97c067d2ba626205ba002118e4636cb8549f6e32b1515cefb8ae7139512L85-R87)

author: mkorje
body:
## Font handling ~~The default math font (new computer modern math) has been added to the text font fallback list. This means that math will always be able to render, as long as the user doesn't `#set text(fallback: false)`.~~ ~~The way in which font fallback in math works is nearly identical to normal text layout. The key difference is that we only use fonts that have a MATH table present, skipping ones that don't. Note that while strings in math don't use the text font, they do go through normal text layout. So `$🍏$` will render as a tofu, whereas `$"🍏"$` will not.~~ Math layout will fallback through all available fonts, and has its own set of fallback fonts distinct from normal text.
Test changes caused by font handling --- **math-font-fallback**: Font fall back in math only goes through fonts with a MATH table. | Old | New | | - | - | | ![math-font-fallback-old](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b61bffa-b5d9-433e-a0a4-c89e63486059) | ![math-font-fallback-new](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e447edf-bbad-42d0-97e7-aa48f081cfe8) | ```typ --- math-font-fallback --- // Test font fallback. $ よ and "よ" and 🏳️‍🌈 $ ``` --- **math-lr-scripts**: The `zws` is now just ignored, so it no longer removes the spacing after the `lr`. (i.e. the test now matches what it would look like if the `zws` weren't there.) | Old | New | | - | - | | ![math-lr-scripts-old](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c52881f7-c6ca-4f75-98db-25c3356a593c) | ![math-lr-scripts-new](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a4dafaa-d5ba-4d26-aa3b-157a2b8a4ce1) | ```typ --- math-lr-scripts --- // Test interactions with script attachments. $ lr(size: #3em, |)_a^b lr(size: #3em, zws|)_a^b lr(size: #3em, [x])_0^1 [x]_0^1 lr(size: #1em, lr(size: #10em, [x]))_0^1 $ ``` ---
## Repr in math `RawElem` in math is kinda weird. At the moment it basically ends up going through `layout_external` since the font has changed: https://github.com/typst/typst/blob/0a3c6939dd274f40672484695d909c2cc0d0d755/crates/typst-layout/src/math/mod.rs#L474-L481 To preserve this behaviour, I've opted to cut any processing of `RawElem` off during realisation in math mode and add a check to not set the baseline for a `RawElem`. ## Multiple fonts in math As the name of the PR would suggest, multiple fonts now just work in math. No need for `box` hacks anymore.
New tests as examples --- **math-font-features-switch**: You can use glyphs from a font's stylistic sets now. Notice that the math kerning with the subscripts is still working! ![math-font-features-switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3128266d-0cd8-4a6a-9dd8-4310576f435e) ```typ --- math-font-features-switch --- #let scr(it) = text(features: ("ss01",), $cal(it)$) $cal(P)_i != scr(P)_i$, $cal(bold(I))_l != bold(scr(I))_l$ $ product.co_(B in scr(B))^(B in scr(bold(B))) cal(B)(X) $ ``` --- **math-font-covers**: You can use covers with fonts in math now, so that specific glyphs are from a given font. Again, notice the kerning with the subscripts. ![math-font-covers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5aa1131-b881-4408-b941-acf7538d9bbe) ```typ --- math-font-covers --- #show math.equation: set text( font: ( // Ignore that this regex actually misses some of the script glyphs... (name: "XITS Math", covers: regex("[\u{1D49C}-\u{1D503}]")), ), features: ("ss01",), ) $ cal(P)_i (X) * cal(C)_1 $ ``` --- **math-op-font**: You can use any font you'd like operators and limits will work as specified. ![math-op-font](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21e3ad3f-db3c-44d4-ad15-dd5695e995f7) ```typ --- math-op-font --- // Test with different font. #let colim = math.op( text(font: "IBM Plex Sans", weight: "regular", size: 0.8em)[colim], limits: true, ) $ colim_(x -> 0) inline(colim_(x -> 0)) $ ``` --- **math-op-set-font**: Notice the improved kerning between the letters in each operator (less space between `c` and `h` in `sech`, more space between `o` and `d` in `mod`) as well as the ligature. ```typ --- math-op-set-font --- // Test setting font. #show math.equation: set text(weight: "regular") #let lig = math.op("fi") #let test = $sech(x) mod_(x -> oo) lig_1(X)$ #test #show math.op: set text(font: "New Computer Modern") #test ``` ---
## More customisation and control Whenever a glyph is laid out in math by Typst (e.g. the delims for matrices, the accent glyph for accents), it now goes through realisation. Essentially, this means you can now target them with show rules. Combine this with proper support for multiple fonts, and you can do all sorts of stuff (even very cursed things)!
New tests as examples --- **math-root-show-rule-1** ```typ --- math-root-show-rule-1 --- #show "√": set text(red, font: "Noto Sans Math") $ root(2, (a + b) / c) $ ``` --- **math-root-show-rule-2** ```typ --- math-root-show-rule-2 --- #show "√": set text(2em) $ sqrt(2) $ ``` --- **math-root-show-rule-3** ```typ --- math-root-show-rule-3 --- // Test cursed show rule. #show "√": "!" $ sqrt(2) root(2, 2) $ ``` --- **math-root-show-rule-4** ```typ --- math-root-show-rule-4 --- #show math.root: set text(red) $ sqrt(x + y) root(4, 2) $ ``` --- **math-root-show-rule-5** ```typ --- math-root-show-rule-5 --- #show math.root: it => { show "√": set text(purple) if it.index == none it } $ sqrt(1/2) root(3, 1/2) $ ``` --- **math-delim-show-rule-1** ```typ --- math-delim-show-rule-1 --- #show regex("\[|\]"): set text(green, font: "Noto Sans Math") $ mat(delim: \[, a, b, c; d, e, f; g, h, i) quad [x + y] $ ``` --- **math-delim-show-rule-2** ```typ --- math-delim-show-rule-2 --- #show math.vec: it => { show regex("\(|\)"): set text(blue) it } $ vec(1, 0, 0), mat(1; 0; 0), (1), binom(n, k) $ ``` --- **math-delim-show-rule-3** ```typ --- math-delim-show-rule-3 --- #show "⏟": set text(fuchsia) $ underbrace(1 + 1 = 2, "obviously") $ ``` --- **math-delim-show-rule-4** ```typ --- math-delim-show-rule-4 --- #show "{": set text(navy) $ cases(x + y + z = 0, 2x - y = 0, -5y + 2z = 0) $ ``` --- **math-delim-show-rule-5**

author: raymar9
body:
Due to Python package dependency issues with newer Python versions and the current inadequate way how Python dependencies are installed when using the Debian packages, we moved to poetry and reworked the whole packaging process.

Now,

- poetry is directly used for generating the Python wheel and source package
- shiv is used to bundle the Python package and all its Python dependencies in a self-contained .pyz file
- which is packaged together with the existing systemd service file in a Debian package

body:
## #️⃣ Issue Number

<!--- ex) #이슈번호, #이슈번호 -->
#47 

## 📝 요약(Summary)

<!--- 변경 사항 및 관련 이슈에 대해 간단하게 작성해주세요. 어떻게보다 무엇을 왜 수정했는지 설명해주세요. -->
- 장소 상세 정보 조회 API를 개발하였습니다.

- tagType(MOOD, SOLO)을 기준으로 가장 많이 선택된 태그 이름순으로 태그 이름과 선택빈도를 반환하도록 하는 메서드
```java
  @Query(
      """
            SELECT new com.ilta.solepli.domain.solmap.dto.TagInfo(rt.name, COUNT(rt))
            FROM ReviewTag rt
            JOIN rt.review r
            WHERE r.place.id = :placeId AND rt.tagType = :tagType
            GROUP BY rt.name
            ORDER BY COUNT(rt) DESC
            """)
  List<TagInfo> findTagCountsByPlaceAndType(
      @Param("placeId") Long placeId, @Param("tagType") TagType tagType);
``` 

- 리뷰 엔티티에서 reviewImages와 reviewTags 2개 모두 컬렉션이어서 2개 모두 FETCH JOIN이 불가능합니다. 그래서 reviewImages만 FETCH JOIN을 걸고 reviewTags에는 @BatchSize를 추가하여 지연로딩을 하되 최대 10개의 Review 엔티티에 달린 reviewTags를 IN절(batch)로 묶어서 한 번에 조회하도록 하였습니다.

```java
  @OneToMany(mappedBy = "review", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
  @Builder.Default
  @BatchSize(size = 10)
  private List<ReviewTag> reviewTags = new ArrayList<>();
``` 
```java
  @Query(
      """
                      SELECT r
                      FROM Review r
                      JOIN FETCH r.user u
                      JOIN FETCH r.reviewImages ri
                      WHERE r.place.id = :placeId
                      ORDER BY r.createdAt DESC
                  """)
  List<Review> findByWithImagesAndUserByPlaceId(@Param("placeId") Long placeId, Pageable pageable);
```

어떤 변경 사항이 있나요?

- [X] 새로운 기능 추가

author: derpbravely
body:
## Description

Select and combobox refactor

## Changes

- Code separation for Select components
- Move and merge common list box types (Option/Item/Section definitions) to the list box folder

## Additional information

Sections in list boxes are [documented by react aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/ListBox.html#dynamic-items) like:

```ts
const items = [
  {
    // No id for the section
    name: 'Frukter',
    children: [
      {
        id: 1,
        name: 'Banan'
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

```tsx
<ComboBox {...props}>
  {/* The section needs an ID, since it is not defined in the data we set it from the name attribute */}
  {section => <ComboBoxSection {...section} id={section.name} />}
</ComboBox>
```

This is how we do it in the `Select` component and I think we should be doing it in the `ComboBox` aswell, now we offer additional attributes on the `ListBoxSectionElement` type to avoid breaking changes, but the documentation is updated according to React Arias way of doing it.

## Checklist
- [x] Iterate variable names

author: ibrahim-haizel
body:
---

## Add WhatsNew Svelte Component and Integrate Homepage Updates Section

---

## Overview

This pull request introduces a new, flexible `WhatsNew` Svelte component designed to serve as a reusable changelog/news section. The component is integrated into the homepage, providing a clear and accessible way of communicating recent updates, releases, and important announcements. Supporting example wrappers and documentation code snippets have also been added.

---

## Motivation & Context

- Provides a standardised, visually consistent news and updates component for use across multiple pages or sites.
- Ensures users are kept up-to-date with the latest changes in a prominent, accessible format.
- Improves developer experience by documenting usage through examples and code blocks.
- Aligns with GOV.UK designs system

---

## Changes in Detail

### 1. New Component: WhatsNew

- **File:** `src/lib/components/ui/WhatsNew.svelte`
- **Description:**  
  A new, reusable Svelte component implementing a visually prominent "What's New" or "Changelog" section, with:
  - Customisable title, section ID, intro text, and an array of news items.
  - Each news item supports: date, content, optional release notes link and version, and bulleted lists of related component links.
  - Accessible markup and GOV.UK-compliant styling.
  - Documented props and usage examples.

---

### 2. Homepage Integration

- **File:** `src/routes/+page.svelte`
- **Description:**  
  The homepage now features the new `<WhatsNew>` component, displaying the most recent updates and release information for the library.
- **Key changes:**
  - Imports and renders `<WhatsNew>` with tailored news items and intro text.
  - Ensures the updates section is visually distinct and easy to find.

---

### 3. Documentation & Examples

- **Files:**
  - `src/wrappers/components/ui/WhatsNewWrapper.svelte`
  - `src/wrappers/components/ui/whats-new/Examples.svelte`
  - `src/wrappers/components/ui/whats-new/codeBlocks.js`
- **Description:**  
  Provides wrapper and example files for documentation and developer onboarding:
  - **`Examples.svelte`**: Interactive accordion with several usage demonstrations and rendered code blocks.
  - **`codeBlocks.js`**: Svelte code snippets for documentation and copy-paste usage.
  - **`WhatsNewWrapper.svelte`**: For documented preview of the WhatsNew component.

---

## How it Works

- **Props Interface:**
  - `title` (string): Section heading (default: "What's new")
  - `titleId` (string): HTML id for heading (for anchor links)
  - `componentLinksIntroText` (string): Intro text for component links list
  - `newsItems` (array): List of news items with optional details (date, content, release notes, version, component links)
- **Rendering:**
  - Iterates through `newsItems`, displaying each with date, content, and (optionally) release notes and bulleted lists of related components.
  - Styles and layout match GOV.UK Design System conventions.
- **Accessibility:**
  - Uses semantic heading structure, accessible link text, and clear sectioning.
  - Supports screen readers with appropriate markup and alt text where required.
- **Customisation:**
  - Props are typed and have sensible defaults, allowing for both quick setup and advanced use cases.

---

## How to Test

1. **Homepage:**  
   - Visit the homepage and confirm the new WhatsNew section appears with the correct title and the latest updates.
   - Check that links to release notes and component documentation are present where expected.
   - Confirm visual styling aligns with GOV.UK patterns, and layout is responsive.
2. **Component API:**  
   - Try using `<WhatsNew>` elsewhere with different props to verify flexibility.
3. **Documentation/Playground:**  
   - Navigate to the component docs/playground to view example props and rendered variants.
4. **Accessibility:**  
   - Verify headings, links, and lists are correctly marked up and usable with assistive technologies.

---

## Checklist

- [ ] Component props are documented and have sensible defaults.
- [ ] Styles scoped and responsive.
- [ ] Integration tested on homepage.
- [ ] Documentation and examples updated.
- [ ] Accessibility reviewed.

---

## Related Issues

- _None directly referenced, but this PR helps establish a consistent pattern for communicating updates and changelogs across the project and is part of wider design ticket._

## Further Work

- Add more diverse usage examples and edge cases to documentation.
- Gather feedback for additional features or improvements to the WhatsNew API.

---

**Reviewer notes:**  
- Please review the prop API and suggest improvements for flexibility or accessibility if needed.
- Feedback on the styling, and structure is welcome.

---

In vlcluster evel setups, components like vlselect can still accept and forward /insert requests. The lack of strict endpoint control increases the risk of human error and undermines deployment security boundaries.

See https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/issues/143

Add flags to disable the vlinsert and vlselect endpoints. The `-insert.disable` flag also disables the internalinsert endpoint. Similarly for vlselect.

author: chibie
body:
## Overview
This PR merges the stable branch into main, introducing a new transactions system with enhanced security features and improved data management capabilities.

## Key Changes

### 1. New Transactions Table Implementation
- Created a new `transactions` table in Supabase with comprehensive schema
- Added support for multiple transaction types (swap, transfer)
- Implemented JSONB storage for flexible recipient data structure
- Added proper indexing for performance optimization

### 2. Enhanced Security Features
- Implemented Row Level Security (RLS) policies
- Added wallet address validation and normalization
- Introduced rate limiting for API endpoints
- Created secure transaction ownership verification

### 3. New API Endpoints
- Added transaction management endpoints:
  - GET `/api/v1/transactions` - List transactions with pagination
  - GET `/api/v1/transactions/address/:address` - Get transactions by address
  - POST `/api/v1/transactions` - Create new transaction
  - PUT `/api/v1/transactions/[id]` - Update transaction details
  - PUT `/api/v1/transactions/status/[id]` - Update transaction status

### 4. Frontend Integration
- Added new `TransactionsContext` for state management
- Implemented transaction history view with pagination
- Added transaction status reconciliation
- Integrated with wallet connection system

### 5. Data Management Improvements
- Added transaction caching mechanism
- Implemented background status reconciliation
- Added proper error handling and logging
- Introduced transaction status tracking

## Technical Details

### Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE transactions (
    id uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
    wallet_address TEXT NOT NULL,
    transaction_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (transaction_type IN ('swap', 'transfer')),
    from_currency TEXT NOT NULL,
    to_currency TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount_sent NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    amount_received NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    fee NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    recipient JSONB NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'completed', 'failed')),
    tx_hash TEXT,
    time_spent TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()) NOT NULL,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()) NOT NULL
);
```

### Security Features
- Row Level Security (RLS) policies ensure users can only access their own transactions
- Wallet address validation prevents unauthorized access
- Rate limiting protects against abuse
- Secure transaction ownership verification

## Testing
- Added comprehensive test coverage for new endpoints
- Implemented transaction flow testing
- Added security policy verification
- Tested rate limiting functionality

## Dependencies
- Updated various package dependencies for improved security and performance
- Added new dependencies for transaction management
- Updated TypeScript types for better type safety

## Migration Notes
- No data migration required
- New table will be created automatically
- Existing code will continue to work with new implementation

## Documentation
- Added comprehensive API documentation
- Updated transaction flow documentation
- Added security policy documentation
- Included setup and testing instructions

author: ostrzyciel
body:
Issue: #406 

This removes LazyProperty and LastNodeHolder classes, which serve to simply hold references to other objects and wrap the logic for accessing them.

Unfortunately, they are also used in a hot path, and each of these objects adds 16 bytes of heap usage and possibly additional pointer math. The more significant part is the 16 bytes, because that takes up cache lines, and cache throughput is our main bottleneck.

I've simply unrolled these objects, putting the relevant access logic in the containing classes, as private methods.

I wrote a benchmark for ProtoDecoder that uses real data from the assist-iot-weather dataset, with 100k triples.

Here are the key changes:
- I updated `manifest.json` by adding the `nativeMessaging` permission, a background script, and a native messaging host definition. I also bumped the version to 0.2.0.
- I added `background.js` to manage the connection and message relay between the content script and the native Python host.
- I modified `content_script.js` to send detected requests to `background.js` and listen for responses to inject into the Gemini chat interface. This includes placeholder DOM selectors for Gemini's input and send button.
- I added `mcp_native_host.py`, a Python script that listens for requests from the extension via stdio, prints them, and includes a commented-out example for sending responses back.
- I added `mcp_native_host_manifest.json`, which is a manifest file for Firefox to discover and run the Python native messaging host.
- I updated `README.md` to provide comprehensive setup instructions for both the extension and the native messaging components. This includes Python script preparation, native host manifest registration for Windows, Linux, and macOS, and debugging advice.

This architecture allows for more complex processing of requests outside the browser environment and enables bidirectional communication between the extension and the Python script.

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve configuration clarity and code documentation, restructure docs, and introduce YouTube upload support.

New Features:
- Integrate YouTube uploading with playlist support via new YouTubeUpload, YouTubeHelper, and YtStatus classes.
- Allow dynamic upload destination selection (GDrive, Rclone, YouTube) with raw_up_dest tracking and user ‘upload_dest’ settings menu.

- Restructure startup and configuration loading to log database connections, load settings, and update global variables.

Build:

author: demesmaeker
body:
Currently, the feature to manage a discount based on the cheapest
product doesn't make a lot of sense. It's always the cheapest product
of the order, applied as many times as needed. Disregarding the fact that
a buyer that read the thin prints would separate their order in
multiple orders to gain the more money as possible.

E.g.: if you need to buy 2 products to receive the promotion to get 50% on
the cheapest, and you have 3 products to buy: A desk (€950), a chair
(€60), and a pack of gums (€0.99). They buyer could either make an order
of these 3 products and receive a discount of €0.49, or make a first
order of the desk and the table, with a discount of €30, and then a last
order with the pack of gums, without any discount. So the "cheapest" as
being the cheapest of the order didn't make a lot of sense.

Another problem was, when using the cheapest reward more than once, that
you could discount that single product for more than its value.

E.g.: same case, but 3 desks (€950 each), 11 chairs (€60 each) and a pack
of gums (€0.99). The reward got applied 7 times.
Before this commit, the order's discount in the POS would be €3.47
(7\*0.99\*0.5), disregarding the fact that that pack of gum couldn't be
discounted for more than its value.
Or the buyer could make 3 orders to get the best discount. First 2
desks (50% on a desk), then a desk and 11 chairs (6 times 50% on a chair)
and finally, that pack of gum, for a total discount of €655.

After this commit, the buyer could get the same result in a single order.

In order to allow promotion programs such as: "Buy a desk, get 10% on
the 4th chair", it was decided to use a new repeater field instead of
the reward's required points to count the step before applying the next
reward.

body:
## 🚀 Pull Request: Upgrade to .NET 9 + Secure Connection String via `.env`

### 📌 Summary

This PR introduces two key improvements:

1. **Upgraded project to target .NET 9.0** with C# 13 support.
2. **Moved the database connection string to a `.env` file** for improved security and flexibility in configuration management.

---

### ✅ What's Changed

#### 🔧 Framework Upgrade

* **Target Framework**: Changed from previous version (e.g., .NET 8) to **`.NET 9.0`**.
* **LangVersion**: Set to **C# 13** for access to latest language features.

#### 🔐 Configuration Refactor

* **Moved connection string** from `appsettings.json` to **`.env`** file:

  * Created `.env` for actual use.
  * Added `.env.example` for development reference.
* **Updated `Program.cs`**:

  * Integrated `DotNetEnv` to load environment variables.
  * Ensured that environment variables are added to `IConfiguration`.
* **Modified `Infrastructure.DependencyInjection`**:

  * Now uses `configuration["DefaultConnection"]` to read from environment variables.

#### 🧹 Cleanup

* Removed the `ConnectionStrings` section from `appsettings.json`.
* Updated `.gitignore` to exclude `.env` from version control.

---

### 📂 File Changes Summary

| File                     | Change Type | Description                                       |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `*.csproj`               | ✨ Updated   | TargetFramework set to `net9.0`, LangVersion `13` |
| `.env`                   | ➕ Added     | Stores `DefaultConnection` string                 |
| `.env.example`           | ➕ Added     | Template file with placeholder values             |
| `appsettings.json`       | 🗑️ Cleaned | Removed `ConnectionStrings` section               |
| `Program.cs`             | ✏️ Updated  | Loads `.env` and adds env vars to config          |
| `DependencyInjection.cs` | ✏️ Updated  | Uses `configuration["DefaultConnection"]`         |

---

### 🔒 Why This Is Better

* **Security**: Keeps secrets out of version-controlled files.
* **Flexibility**: Different environments (dev/stage/prod) can use their own `.env` files.
* **Modernization**: Leverages .NET 9.0 and C# 13 features.

---

### 🧪 Testing

* Verified DB connection works via `.env`.
* Confirmed `.env` is not tracked by Git.
* Ensured app builds and runs under .NET 9.0 SDK.

### Work done

- Created a test Lua cryptography module to test some libs integrated into engine.
- Totally not for merging atm since it's not even really implemented, but once we choose the crypto lib and decide an api this is the foundation for implementing the module easily.
  - It does use the libraries and return some values to lua :D (see testing below)

#### Related issues

Use these to discuss:

- https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/RecoilEngine/issues/2353
- https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/RecoilEngine/issues/2352

Game need related issues:

- https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/Beyond-All-Reason/issues/5173

### Remarks

- Idea is to figure out what crypto libraries we'd like to integrate into engine and then work on a Lua module.
  - Not much sense in working on this further before we're sure what libraries to use.
- A crypto module should support public key encryption with DH exchange too, and then symmetric encryption.
- Games can then use that to do the following if they so desire:
  - Send confidential information to the server.
  - Store information in the users hard drive in encrypted form only accessible once a password has been entered (normally one would have a password that decrypts a derived secret that's actually what the server uses for multiplayer).
  - Maintain confidential communications with other players or team (with team it can be more complicated xd).
- Idea is go with elliptic curves, since they allow for compact and very efficient cryptography.
- This is just a very early WIP since it's just some test functions accessible from Lua:
  - Crypto.TestEcdsa: secp256k1 signatures test
  - Crypto.TestEcdh: secp256k1 diffie hellman test
  - Crypto.TestAes: cryptopp aes test
  - Crypto.TestTinyAes: tinyaes test (this one actually fails, unsure why)
- Why these libraries?? Ofc not using all, we should either use cryptopp for everything or some other combination.
  - See https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/RecoilEngine/issues/2353 for further information and discussion
  - Initially wanted to try secp256k1 + tinyaes for very lightweight implementation with very specific curves and codecs
  - On the other hand cryptopp is a very complete library, so could use only that one to have most actual cryptographic operations accessible.
  - Added my own fork of cryptopp-cmake (just cmake files), since the current version seems to have a problem that doesn't allow to use it otherwise: https://github.com/abdes/cryptopp-cmake/issues/125


### Testing

add the following at some synced gadget (only linked it at SyncedHandle for testing):

```lua
        if Crypto then
                Spring.Echo("CRYPTO ECDSA", Crypto.TestEcdsa())
                --> CRYPTO ECDSA, A0Jda/N7D+leK0sZ8QY3PIZgrBEB9u1L9esk3QPk9uOv, 4tfe8Y5Ka4qN+wjVExy+R8pCffJOExAh/cDvwGkPMXgL, true

                Spring.Echo("CRYPTO ECDH", Crypto.TestEcdh())
                --> CRYPTO ECDH, A3tdv0R4HneEEwpKNZwW3uyiiCbiZVRgf0nd7vp1ysui

                Spring.Echo("CRYPTO AES", Crypto.TestAes())
                --> CRYPTO AES, true, 332B0E44865B98F27FDE6B203BA6703A

                --> CRYPTO AES, 1, oSsDhtgVosGOnCO2Onrb8v1VduyJtkvvj/8gxnottSXW3fqO/XsPzYaf/oRWTmA+bfllrg3Ibgl73ym/qkXNVw==, 9YxMBNbl8bp3nqv7X3v71pz8TpZ+24CNZ593e8ZwLH058jNpqdm6z6Uw4mMEIxRhsusF4sOb6fzabBkHjGqdGw==, false

author: bobelchev
body: ## 🔄 Pull Request: Refactor Monolith into Decoupled Kafka-Based Microservices ### 📌 Summary This PR refactors the existing monolithic architecture into a modular, service-oriented design using **Apache Kafka** as a message broker between two Spring Boot services. --- ### 🧱 New Architecture #### 1. `kraken-ws-service` (Kafka Producer) - Connects to Kraken's WebSocket V2 API. - Subscribes to selected crypto trading pairs. - Publishes real-time ticker data to a Kafka topic. #### 2. `crypto-trading-service` (Kafka Consumer) - Subscribes to the Kafka topic to receive live market data. - Handles all other application logic, including: - Market data processing - WebSocket connections with frontend clients - Pushes live updates to connected frontend users. #### 3. Apache Kafka & Zookeeper (via Docker) - Kafka acts as the messaging backbone. - Zookeeper supports Kafka coordination. - Docker images used for local development and testing. --- ### 🏗️ Architectural Transition #### 🧱 Previous Architecture (Monolith) > A single service handled: > - Kraken WebSocket connection > - Market data processing > - Frontend WebSocket communication --- #### 🧱 New Architecture (Decoupled Microservices) > Responsibilities are now split between two independent services, communicating through Kafka: > - Promotes modularity and clean separation of concerns > - Supports independent deployment and scaling --- ### ✅ Benefits - 🔁 **Loose coupling** between producer and consumer - 📈 **Scalability**: Services can scale independently - 🧪 **Testability**: Easier to test services in isolation - 📦 **Extensibility**: Easy to add new consumers (e.g., analytics, persistence layer) ---

author: leanserra
body:
**Motivation**

We want to prove execution of blocks by recording an execution witness that returns all the minimal necessary data to perform stateless execution. 

**Description**

- Merge ProverDB with ExecutionWitnessResult
   -  ExecutionWitnessResult implements `VmDatabase` to be used with the EVM
   - on the prover side
     - ExecutionWitnessResult is used as the db, all operations are made with the pruned MPT so there is no need for verify_db 
     - The trie is modified as blocks are executed so no need to update tries at the end of execution either
   - on the ethrex_replay side
     - remove old code used to prove block execution with eth_getProof and debug_getRawBlock
     - use ExecutionWitnessResult for proving

**How to test**

#### ethrex_replay `cd cmd/ethrex_replay/`
- With a synced l1 ethrex instance (it can also be tested with dev mode l1 `make init-l1` but blocks are mostly empty) :

```Shell
cargo run --release -- execute block --rpc-url "http://localhost:8545" 1
```

- Test a single transaction 

```Shell
cargo run --release -- execute tx --rpc-url "http://localhost:8545" <tx-hash>
```

#### l2 proving

- Run an L2 integration test

author: eps1lon
body:
We now enforce via ESLint that `require()` calls in `packages/**/*.tsx?` expose the types of the underlying module via `require(source) as typeof import(source)`.

The rule has an autofixer so all you have to do is write `require(source)` and get completions for `require(source) as typeof import(source)`.

When moving files, TS would adjust the `import(source)` so when the lint rules finds mismatches like `require(requireSource) as typeof import(importSource)`, we'll favor `importSource` i.e. will autofix to `require(importSource) as typeof import(importSource)`.

I disabled the lint rule for the scenarios where I didn't feel comfortable moving to relative imports e.g. https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/80056/files#diff-21d0b6f147bdd2dba7964674d5b7a9e3f2b7e2c4d1e5e5423069d9ea2dfe1a6fR13-R15

author: suibianp
body:
`runInTerminal` is currently implemented using JSON messages over FIFOs, which feels too clunky for the simple job of passing a PID.

Instead, take advantage of `si_pid` available from `sa_sigaction` handler, and send a user signal instead. Both synchronisation and timeout are preserved with the protocol below,

1. Debugger waits for `SIGUSR1` under timeout with pselect
2. Launcher forks into child, sends `SIGUSR1` to debugger and suspends
3. Debugger receives `SIGUSR1`, captures the sender (launcher child) PID, attaches to and resumes it
4. Launcher child resumes and `exec`'s into target
5. Launcher parent `waitpid`'s and kills irresponsive child after timeout

With this, the entirety of `FifoFiles` and `RunInTerminal` can be dropped.

Refs: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/121269#issuecomment-2901401482

Overview
----------------------------------------
Possible fix for https://lab.civicrm.org/dev/core/-/issues/5926 . It seems broken as far back as 6.2 to me.

Before
----------------------------------------
Editing a File type custom field on a case hangs - it can't handle rendering new vs old value for the "Change Custom Data" activity.

After
----------------------------------------
File URIs are saved in the Case Data Changed activity.

Technical Details
----------------------------------------
Beware browser caching when testing URLs when the source image changes on the server...

Comments
----------------------------------------
There seem to be a few things going wrong here.

Immediate issue = array values are being passed to functions that expect strings/ints, and things being in different keys between quickform / api3 / bao layers.

Bigger picture issues
- it seems that case file change maintain the same file ID, which messes with trying to render before/after values, as generated URLs will all point to the latest file.
- file urls with checksums are time limited anyway, so saving them permanently in the body of these Activities isn't going to work anyway. I think we'd need some special handling to save the before/after file ID, then render checksum-ed links dynamically
- it's not clear to me what the expected behaviour is when changing files. Would you expect the old one to be deleted? Or a permanent record created?

body:
# Enhance Stripe Checkout URL Detection for Preview Deployments

## Problem
Following up on PR #69, the Stripe checkout URL detection needed enhancement to properly handle Vercel preview deployments. Currently, preview branches would fall back to the production URL (`https://vargasjr.dev`) instead of using the specific preview deployment URL.

## Solution
Enhanced the base URL detection logic in `/app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` to include `VERCEL_URL` environment variable support for preview deployments.

## Changes
- Updated URL detection priority to: `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` → `VERCEL_URL` → production/development URLs
- Added `process.env.VERCEL_URL` check with proper HTTPS protocol prefix
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing production and development environments

## URL Priority Logic
1. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`** - Explicit override (highest priority)
2. **`VERCEL_URL`** - Preview deployment URL (e.g., `vargasjr-dev-git-branch-name-david-vargas.vercel.app`)
3. **Production** - `https://vargasjr.dev` when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`
4. **Development** - `http://localhost:3000` for local development

## Testing
- ✅ `npm run lint` - No ESLint warnings or errors
- ✅ `npm t` - All tests pass

- Implements suggestion from [PR #69 comment](https://github.com/dvargas92495/vargasjr-dev/pull/69#issuecomment-2927104869)

author: twlqcd
body:
The lack of constraints on the template parameters for the non-member overloaded operators for Kokkos::complex can create issues when defining overloads between Kokkos::complex and user-defined classes. An example of where this can arise is with expression templates, e.g a scaling of an user-defined class:

alpha * x

with alpha a Kokkos::complex and x an user-defined class. The compiler tries to force an object of the user defined class into the constructor of Kokkos::complex when returning the result of the operation.

This PR constrains the template parameters of the non-member operator overloads to only accept arithmetic types, which resolves the aforementioned issue.

author: malston
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive GitHub release asset download feature for the release monitor, adding the ability to automatically download release assets when new versions are detected.

## Changes Made

### Phase 1: Core Components
- **Version Database** (`github_version_db.py`): Thread-safe version tracking with file locking
- **Version Comparison** (`version_compare.py`): Intelligent version comparison supporting SemVer, CalVer, and custom formats
- **Unit Tests**: Comprehensive test coverage for core components

### Phase 2: Download Functionality  
- **GitHub Downloader** (`github_downloader.py`): Core download functionality with retry logic and verification
- **Download Coordinator** (`download_releases.py`): Main coordination script for processing releases
- **Bash Wrapper** (`scripts/download.sh`): User-friendly command-line interface
- **Unit Tests**: Download functionality test coverage

### Phase 3: Integration & Testing
- **Monitor Integration**: Added `--download` flag to `github_monitor.py`
- **Configuration**: Extended `config.yaml` with comprehensive download settings
- **Integration Tests**: End-to-end testing scenarios (`tests/integration/test_monitor_download.py`)
- **Documentation**: Complete user guide (`DOWNLOAD_GUIDE.md`)

### Phase 4: Concourse Pipeline Integration
- **Full Pipeline** (`ci/pipeline-with-downloads.yml`): S3-based pipeline with download capabilities
- **Simple Pipeline** (`ci/pipeline-downloads-simple.yml`): Local download pipeline without S3
- **Deployment Guide**: Comprehensive Concourse deployment documentation
- **README Updates**: Pipeline options and integration examples

## Key Features

- ✅ **Smart Version Management**: Tracks downloaded versions to prevent duplicates
- ✅ **Asset Filtering**: Download specific files using configurable glob patterns
- ✅ **Organized Storage**: Files organized by repository and version (`downloads/owner/repo/version/`)
- ✅ **Retry Logic**: Automatic retry on download failures with configurable attempts
- ✅ **Verification**: Optional SHA256 checksum verification for downloaded files
- ✅ **Concurrency**: Configurable concurrent downloads for performance
- ✅ **Integration**: Seamless integration with existing monitor functionality
- ✅ **Concourse Support**: Multiple pipeline options for different deployment scenarios

## Configuration Example

```yaml
download:
  enabled: true
  directory: ./downloads
  version_db: ./version_db.json
  asset_patterns:
    - "*.tar.gz"
    - "*.zip"
    - "\!*-sources.zip"
  verify_checksums: true
  retry_attempts: 3
  retry_delay: 2
  max_concurrent: 4
```

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Monitor and download new releases
python3 github_monitor.py --config config.yaml --download

# Download from existing monitor output
python3 download_releases.py --config config.yaml --input releases.json

# Using the bash wrapper
./scripts/monitor.sh --download
./scripts/download.sh --input releases.json
```

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for version comparison and database operations
- [x] Unit tests for download functionality and error handling  
- [x] Integration tests for monitor with download feature
- [x] Manual testing with real GitHub repositories
- [x] Concourse pipeline validation
- [x] Documentation review and examples testing

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a backward-compatible addition that doesn't affect existing functionality.

## Dependencies

No new external dependencies added. Uses existing `requests` and `PyYAML` libraries.

## Documentation

- [Download Guide](DOWNLOAD_GUIDE.md) - Comprehensive usage documentation
- [Concourse Deployment Guide](CONCOURSE_DEPLOYMENT.md) - Pipeline deployment instructions  
- [README.md](README.md) - Updated with download feature overview
- Integration tests with usage examples

This pull request introduces significant improvements to deployment scripts and workflows, focusing on better error handling, enhanced logging, and streamlined processes for installing and starting services. It also includes updates to the GitHub Actions workflow for improved configuration and cleanup.

### Deployment Script Enhancements

* [`.deploy/install-services.sh`](diffhunk://#diff-ef13621a671ee63559ad6f0fcab23472b47932cc84e412cc1ecfb1c5dda58287R2-R98): Refactored the script to use a `run_sudo` helper for conditional passwordless `sudo` execution, added detailed logging messages, improved Docker installation and error handling, and included checks for Docker and Nginx versions.

* [`.deploy/start-services.sh`](diffhunk://#diff-94396e1fa6a5a1e8d565d910decf21a053d3fa75d7b71d816c038b8ea0cb43d6L5-R17): Modified the script to accept GitHub token and username as parameters, added checks for Docker login and image pulling failures, improved health checks for containers, and enhanced logging for service readiness. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-94396e1fa6a5a1e8d565d910decf21a053d3fa75d7b71d816c038b8ea0cb43d6L5-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-94396e1fa6a5a1e8d565d910decf21a053d3fa75d7b71d816c038b8ea0cb43d6R34-R88)

### GitHub Actions Workflow Updates

* [`.github/workflows/build-and-deploy.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-ecad2183af1362d9d99f4a33e7491c1970c92255c3c318e688ece549ec91fe33R170-R183): Added support for `SUDO_PASSWORD` in the environment, improved Docker installation checks, and streamlined service startup with dynamic environment variables. Removed redundant cleanup and notification steps for failure scenarios. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ecad2183af1362d9d99f4a33e7491c1970c92255c3c318e688ece549ec91fe33R170-R183) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ecad2183af1362d9d99f4a33e7491c1970c92255c3c318e688ece549ec91fe33L209-R211) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ecad2183af1362d9d99f4a33e7491c1970c92255c3c318e688ece549ec91fe33L222-L266)

author: disberd
body:
This PR refactor the code in the ItuRP2145 module to implement the functions for all 4 variables specified within the Recommendation.

It also refactor some internals with the following main changes:
- All instances of the word `vapor` in the codebase has been replaced with `vapour` for consistency to the Recommendation texts
- The `ItuRP2145` module has been refactored to use an independent artifact and for a more modular structure.
- The `ItuRP2145` module now supports computation of average annual values, as opposed to only the CCDF values supported in previous versions
  - The module now also supports computing the total barometric pressure and the integrated water vapour content, available via the `surfacepressureannual` and `surfacewatervapourcontentannual` functions, respectively.
- The function of the `ItuRP2145` module are now tested against the validation examples excel provided by ITU-R.
- A new module `ItuRP1144` has been added to store the interpolation function defined in the ITU-R P.1144-12 recommendation.
  - This module currently only implements the bilinear interpolation on a square grid

author: lzap
body:
Small nitpicks for the paginator, mostly docs, inconsistency for getters (some having the prefix while others dont) and useless memory consumption for count.

It is worth noting that in the review (https://github.com/osbuild/image-builder-crc/pull/1610) I expressed an opinion to avoid getters for the fields alltogether and export all the three fields. The type currently is mutable due to the fact that it does not copy the slice, so exposing those fields does not change a thing about immutability. However, type inference for generics only works with functions, so it would create it a little more verbose which I do not like:

```go
p := common.Paginator[int]{values, limit, offset}
```

Therefore I am not including such a change.

author: isephix
body:
Adjusted `COLOR_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD_MARKER` in
`js/image_processing.js` from 150 to 80.

This change makes the initial identification of "black-ish" pixels in `findMarkerCandidates_color` more selective. The goal is to reduce the likelihood of non-black pixels being included in the initial binary mask, thereby improving the quality of blobs found by the subsequent Connected Components Labeling.

This should help the "center is not black" filter within `findMarkerCandidates_color` to more accurately identify true marker frames (black borders with non-black centers) by starting with cleaner, more genuinely black candidate regions.

Relaxed geometric filters and the center-check logic remain active for ongoing diagnostics.
